extracted.intended_audience: researchers conducting in vivo animal experiments; authors and peer reviewers/editors of animal-research manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting in vivo animal experiments to improve rigor, transparency, and reproducibility in manuscripts and to aid reviewers/readers in assessing reliability of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 1 of the ARRIVE Essential 10: the way the study was designed (groups, controls, experimental units, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the ARRIVE Essential 10 — one of the basic minimum items that must be reported so readers and reviewers can assess the reliability of the findings. Detailed explanations and examples are provided in the full guideline to help with experimental design and bias minimisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 2 of the ARRIVE Essential 10: details on how sample sizes were decided and any calculations used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 minimum reporting requirement. Consulting the guideline during planning helps researchers with sample size determination and statistical analysis considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 3 of the ARRIVE Essential 10: predefined criteria for including or excluding animals/data from analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 item — must be reported to allow assessment of potential bias from selective inclusion/exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 4 of the ARRIVE Essential 10: whether and how animals/groups were randomly allocated to experimental groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential reporting requirement. Guidance in the full document explains methods to minimise allocation bias and how to report them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding/Masking
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 5 of the ARRIVE Essential 10: whether investigators/data analysts were blinded to group allocation during experiments and outcome assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 item — reporting blinding details is necessary for assessing risk of detection/performance bias; examples and explanations are provided in the full guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 6 of the ARRIVE Essential 10: definition and measurement of primary and secondary outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential reporting element. Clear specification of outcomes supports reproducibility and appropriate interpretation of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 7 of the ARRIVE Essential 10: description of statistical analyses used, including models, assumptions and software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 item — complete reporting of statistical methods helps readers assess rigor; the guideline offers advice on analysis and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 8 of the ARRIVE Essential 10: details of the animals used (species, strain, sex, age, weight, source, genetic modification, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential minimum information. Providing these details aids reproducibility and interpretation across studies and species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 9 of the ARRIVE Essential 10: detailed description of procedures (what was done, how, when, where and why).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential reporting requirement. Thorough procedural description enables replication and assessment of study conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 10 of the ARRIVE Essential 10: complete reporting of results for all measured outcomes, including summary statistics and effect sizes with precision measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 item — reporting full results is necessary for readers/reviewers to evaluate findings; examples given in the full guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 11 of the Recommended set: clear, accurate and structured summary of key elements of the study in the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended set that complements the Essential 10; reporting the abstract items represents best practice and provides important context for the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 12 of the Recommended set: scientific background, rationale and context for the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended information to situate the study within existing literature and explain its importance; complements the Essential 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 13 of the Recommended set: explicit statement of objectives, hypotheses, or research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended reporting element; clarifies the aims tested and informs interpretation of outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 14 of the Recommended set: statement of ethical approval and welfare considerations for animal use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended — reporting ethical approvals and oversight strengthens transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and husbandry
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 15 of the Recommended set: details of animal housing, husbandry conditions and environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended reporting to allow assessment of environmental effects on outcomes and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 16 of the Recommended set: details of care, monitoring, analgesia, humane endpoints and welfare interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended reporting to ensure welfare practices are clear and to assess potential impacts on study results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation/ scientific implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 17 of the Recommended set: interpretation of results in context, including limitations and implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended — helps readers understand how results fit into broader scientific knowledge and any caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability/ translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 18 of the Recommended set: discussion of generalisability of findings and potential for translation to other systems or humans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended reporting to aid assessment of external validity and translational relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 19 of the Recommended set: registration of study protocol and access to pre-specified plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended as best practice to increase transparency, reduce selective reporting and allow comparison of planned vs reported analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 20 of the Recommended set: statement on availability of study data and where they can be accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended — sharing data supports reproducibility and secondary analysis; the guideline encourages data accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 21 of the Recommended set: disclosure of competing interests, funding sources and potential conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended reporting to inform readers of possible sources of bias or influence on the research.
